column3: NASB renders “has become like” as “may be compared to” and “a man, a king” as “a king.”
“Fatlings” is rendered “fattened livestock,” and “killed” is “butchered”; NASB adds “all.”
NASB follows the critical text without “having heard”; “was angry” is rendered “was enraged.”
“Thoroughfares of the highways” is rendered “main highways”; NASB adds “there.”
NASB follows the critical text without “take him away.” “Bind his feet and hands” is rendered “bind him hand and foot.”
“Took counsel” is rendered “plotted together,” and “in His words” is “in what He said.”
NASB renders “there is no care to You about anyone” as “defer to no one,” and “You do not look on the appearance of men” as “You are not partial to any.”
NASB renders “the coin of the tribute” as “the coin used for the poll-tax.”
NASB follows the critical text without “the” before “saying,” and puts the clause in parentheses (“who say there is no resurrection”).
NASB renders “will marry” as “as next of kin shall marry” and prints the quotation in capitals.
NASB renders “err” as “are mistaken” and “knowing” as “understanding.”
NASB follows the critical text with “angels in heaven” (no “of God”).
